info.name: Search Manager API
info.description: Customer-first examples for exploring Search Manager's public Search, Autocomplete, and Analytics endpoints. Start with Start Here. API-key enforcement, index scope, and tracking availability come from the running installation; users never declare a mode or edition. Developer Validation — Optional is isolated and intended only for disposable local fixtures.

exec: console.warn('base_url must be an absolute URL, for example https://example.com.');

item.name: Start Here
item.description: Set base_url and replace query with text known to exist in indexed content. public_api_key is optional unless the running installation requires it. No index is sent: the server searches all enabled indices when enforcement is off, or the public key's allowed indices when enforcement is on.

item.name: Analytics
item.description: The running Search Manager edition and settings determine the response. Users do not declare an edition. Track Search distinguishes recorded from accepted-but-not-recorded responses; Track Click proves acceptance only. A 204 with an empty body is the Standard-edition no-op. Any other status is reported as a failure.

exec: pm.test('Track search was accepted', function () { pm.expect(body).to.have.property('success', true); });
pm.test('Track search was recorded', function () { pm.expect(body.tracked).to.eql(true); });
console.info('Track Search was accepted and recorded.');
pm.test('Track search was accepted but not recorded', function () { pm.expect(body.tracked).to.eql(false); });
console.info('Track Search was accepted but not recorded under the current Analytics settings.');
pm.test('Track search returned its tracking disposition', function () { pm.expect.fail('Expected tracked to be true or false.'); });
